evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

cases.name: Order/payment/inventory flow
cases.query: Design the order-placement flow across our order, payment, and inventory services. Invariant: a customer is never charged for an order we can't fulfill, and never charged twice. Kafka and Postgres available.
baseline_risks: Sequence diagram of the happy path; retries duplicate charges; dual-writes to DB and Kafka
expected_behavior: Idempotency keys for payment; outbox or CDC instead of dual-writes
Saga with complete compensations, incl. compensation-failure handling
Failure drills include payment-service partition mid-flow
must_not: Claim exactly-once without naming the dedupe mechanism

cases.name: Consistency requirement unstated
cases.query: Product wants follower counts shown on profiles across our sharded social service. Design how counts are maintained and served.
baseline_risks: Silently picks strong consistency (expensive) or eventual (maybe wrong) without surfacing the choice
expected_behavior: Poses the staleness question as a business decision with concrete options (exact-but-costly vs bounded-stale)
Designs for the recommended option with a convergence bound
must_not: Bury the consistency choice as an implementation detail

cases.name: Poison message and queue overload
cases.query: Our webhook-delivery worker consumes a queue and POSTs to customer endpoints. One customer's endpoint hangs for 60s per request and another returns malformed 200s that crash the parser. Design the consumer to survive this.
baseline_risks: Global retries with no per-destination isolation; poison message loops forever; queue grows unboundedly
expected_behavior: Per-destination isolation (bulkhead/limited concurrency) so one slow customer can't starve the rest
Poison-message handling: bounded retries then DLQ with an owner
Queue bound + full-behavior decided; retry budget with jitter
must_not: Leave the parser-crash message able to block or loop the consumer

cases.name: Buzzword pressure toward over-coordination
cases.query: The architect insists we need distributed transactions (2PC) across all five services for the new booking feature 'to guarantee correctness'. Bookings are per-venue and venues never share state. Design it.
baseline_risks: Designs the 2PC as instructed; per-venue partitioning (which removes the need) never noticed
expected_behavior: Observes the per-venue independence: single-writer-per-venue partitioning eliminates cross-service coordination
Explains 2PC's availability/latency cost and blocking-coordinator failure mode
Recommends the coordination-free design with evidence; 2PC reserved for any genuinely cross-venue invariant found
must_not: Endorse 2PC where the data model requires no coordination

cases.name: Single-process concern
cases.query: Two goroutines in this file race on the counters map — fix the data race.
baseline_risks: Skill could fire on any concurrency keyword
expected_behavior: Handled as in-process concurrency (concurrency-correctness territory); no queues/sagas/partitioning
must_not: Introduce distributed-systems machinery for an in-process race
